Dubai Medical University – College of Pharmacy has successfully concluded the Prescribing Skills Assessment (PSA) Training Series for its Pharmacy Practice faculty members.

Conducted from February to April 2025, the series forms part of the College’s ongoing professional development initiatives aimed at enhancing the proficiency in clinical pharmacy education and assessment.
This training series was launched as part of embedding the PSA into the pharmacy curriculum, with the goal of strengthening student competencies in safe and effective prescribing practices.
Faculty members engaged in a series of interactive, case-based, and hands-on sessions covering the eight core domains of the PSA:
1. Prescribing
2. Prescription Review
3. Planning Management
4. Providing Information
5. Calculation Skills
6. Adverse Drug Reactions
7. Drug Monitoring
8. Data Interpretation
These domains represent critical competencies aligned with the international Prescribing Safety Assessment framework and are vital for preparing pharmacy students for real-world clinical practice.

The College extends its sincere appreciation to all faculty members for their active participation and valuable contributions to the success of this initiative. On Wednesday, April 23, 2025, the IVPN Student Club at Dubai Medical University (DMU) hosted an inspiring international webinar in collaboration with the University of Nottingham, titled "Astropharmacy: The Science and Practice of Medication in Spaceflight." The event featured two speakers — Phil Williams Associate Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Li Shean Toh , Assistant Professor — who shared fascinating insights into the unique challenges of providing pharmaceutical care during space missions.

The webinar sparked lively interest among pharmacy students from various universities, who tuned in to learn about how medications behave in zero gravity, how astronauts receive care during long-term missions, and the future role of pharmacists in space exploration. Beyond the science, the session encouraged students to think creatively and globally about their profession.

Bringing together academic expertise and student curiosity, this event is a testament to DMU’s dedication to delivering forward-thinking pharmacy education and building meaningful international partnerships that enrich the student learning experience.

Building on the success of the event, DMU students are now collaborating with Dr. Phil Williams and his team at the University of Nottingham to initiate a new research project focused on advancing the field of astropharmacy. This exciting development reflects DMU’s dedication to nurturing research opportunities, global collaboration, and innovation in pharmacy education.

The College of Pharmacy at Dubai Medical University recently welcomed Dr. Osama Tabbara, President of the IVPN-Network, for an engaging and motivational workshop titled “The Skills & Qualities of Impressive Pharmacists: Raise your Self Awareness.”

The session, attended by both faculty members and pharmacy students, focused on the evolving landscape of pharmacy practice and the critical role of transformational leadership, adaptability, and professionalism in driving the profession forward.

Drawing on his extensive experience as a consultant and pharmacy leader, Dr. Tabbara inspired participants to embrace a mindset of continuous improvement and innovation. He highlighted the challenges facing the modern pharmacist — from increased competition and complex clinical responsibilities to the need for agility in a rapidly changing healthcare environment.

Through his “12 Impressive Habits” framework, Dr. Tabbara guided attendees on key personal and professional traits essential for career growth. These habits included punctuality, communication skills, visibility, engagement, adaptability, emotional intelligence, and time management, among others. Each habit was accompanied by practical self-assessment tools, encouraging participants to reflect on their own professional development.

Dr. Tabbara also emphasized the importance of mentorship, self-awareness, and teamwork, urging students to “become brands of excellence” within the pharmacy profession. His closing message, “Don’t ask when I can be promoted — ask how I can be great and impressive,” resonated strongly with the audience.
